idea.title: The undertaker's dial
idea.summary: Almon Strowger, a Kansas City undertaker, believed an operator was steering his callers away and invented the automatic phone exchange, so calls no longer needed a human go-between.
hookOptions: An undertaker invented the phone dial
He thought the operator stole his customers
Phone dials exist because of a funeral home
Nobody trusted the operator, so he built a dial
sources: Wikipedia: Almon Strowger: Kansas City undertaker who believed operators diverted his business to a competitor; patented the step-by-step switch in 1891.
Wikipedia: Almon Strowger / Strowger switch: first automatic exchange opened in La Porte, Indiana, in 1892.

scenes.say: An undertaker invented the phone dial because he thought an operator was stealing customers.
Almon Strowger ran a funeral business in Kansas City, and he believed the operator sent his callers elsewhere.
Back then, a human operator plugged in every call by hand.
So in 1891, he patented a switch that let callers connect themselves.
No operator needed, just a dial and your finger.
The first exchange like it opened in La Porte, Indiana, in 1892.
Today it's one tap, and a stranger picks up.
